brief: Have n grams of dough and m stuffings; bun type i needs b_i stuffing (a_i available) and c_i dough, worth d_i; plain bun needs c0 dough worth d0. Maximize earnings.
key_idea: Bounded knapsack over dough: stuffing i gives at most a_i/b_i copies; plain bun is unbounded.
solution:
1. dp[w] = max money using at most w grams of dough (init 0).
2. For each stuffing i, cnt=a_i/b_i; repeat cnt times a 0/1 pass: for w=n..c_i: dp[w]=max(dp[w], dp[w-c_i]+d_i).
3. Plain bun: unbounded pass for w=c0..n: dp[w]=max(dp[w], dp[w-c0]+d0).
4. Answer dp[n]. Sizes tiny (n<=1000, cnt<=100, m<=10).
complexity: O(n * sum cnt_i) ~ 1e6 time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Sample: n=10, plain(c=2,d=1); stuff1: cnt=7/3=2,c=2,d=100; stuff2: cnt=4,c=1,d=10.
After stuff1: dp[4..10]=200.
After stuff2 (4 copies, 1 dough each): dp[8]=240, dp[10]=240.
Plain bun: dp[10]=max(240, dp[8]+1=241)=241. Output 241.

brief: Array a (n) and strictly decreasing b (m), k starts at 1. Free op: k++ (k<m). Paid op: remove a prefix of a with sum <= b_k at cost m-k. Min cost to empty a, or -1. n*m<=3e5.
key_idea: f[i][k] = min cost to clear suffix from i with current k; for fixed k always jump to the furthest reachable index (two pointers).
solution:
1. f[n][k]=0 for all k; process k from m down to 1, keeping only arrays for k and k+1.
2. For fixed k, r(i) = largest r with sum a[i..r-1] <= b_k; r is non-increasing as i decreases -> two pointers.
3. f[i][k] = min(f[i][k+1] (if k<m), (m-k) + f[r(i)][k] if r(i)>i).
4. Jumping furthest is optimal because f[.][k] is non-increasing in i (shorter suffix never costs more).
5. Answer f[0][1]; INF -> -1.

brief: n plants of m species on a line (given sorted by position). Place borders so section i holds only species i; min plants to move.
key_idea: Kept plants must have non-decreasing species in position order -> answer = n - longest non-decreasing subsequence.
solution:
1. Read species s_1..s_n (positions only matter for order; read x as string/double and ignore).
2. Compute LNDS with tails array and upper_bound (non-strict).
3. Answer n - LNDS length.
4. (O(n*m) DP dp[i] = 1 + max dp[j<i, s_j<=s_i] also fits n<=5000.)
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

brief: n x m grid (<=100) of '*' and '.'. A star = center + 4 equal rays of length s>=1. Cover exactly the '*' cells with at most n*m stars (overlap allowed) or print -1.
key_idea: Put at every '*' the largest star centered there (if size>=1); if the union of all these still misses some '*', it's impossible.
solution:
1. For each '*' cell, grow s while all four cells at distance s+1 are '*' and inside the grid.
2. If s>=1, record (i+1,j+1,s) and mark its cells (difference arrays per row and per column, or brute force).
3. After all, check every '*' is covered; if not print -1.
4. Else print count and stars (count <= n*m automatically). Stars never cover '.', since rays only use '*' cells.
dry_run:
Own example: 3x3 plus shape .*./***/.*.
Center (2,2): s=1; other '*' cells have s=0.
Marked cells = the 5 plus cells, all '*' covered -> print 1 and '2 2 1'.
If grid were ***/***/***: corner (1,1) can't be covered by any star -> -1.

brief: Array a (n<=6000, a_i<=n). Pick two non-overlapping subsegments of equal length L so each is a permutation of consecutive integers and together they form one consecutive range (2L distinct values). Maximize L (0 if impossible).
key_idea: A good segment of length L with min v is exactly the set {v..v+L-1}; we need good segments with mins v and v+L that are disjoint. Brute force over L with a sliding window.
solution:
1. For each L=1..n/2 slide a window of length L, keeping counts (number of duplicated values) and min/max via monotonic deques.
2. Window is good iff no duplicates and max-min==L-1; for its min v record firstEnd[v]=min end index and lastStart[v]=max start index.
3. For each v with v+L<=n: if both mins exist and firstEnd[v]<lastStart[v+L] or firstEnd[v+L]<lastStart[v], L is achievable.
4. Answer = largest achievable L (not monotone, so test all L).
dry_run:
Own example: a=[2,1,4,3].
L=1: windows [2],[1],[4],[3] all good; v=1 (idx1) and v=2 (idx0) disjoint -> ok.
L=2: [2,1] min1 ends at 1; [1,4] bad; [4,3] min3 starts at 2. v=1,v+L=3: firstEnd[1]=1 < lastStart[3]=2 -> ok.
Answer 2 (matches sample note).

brief: String of n charges +1/-1; for each query [l,r], min number of rods to remove so the alternating sum s_l - s_{l+1} + ... of remaining rods is 0.
key_idea: Answer is only 0, 1 or 2: 0 if alternating sum is 0, 1 if segment length is odd, else 2.
solution:
1. p[i] = p[i-1] + sign_i * (i odd ? 1 : -1) (prefix of alternating sum).
2. For query: S = p[r]-p[l-1] (sign flip doesn't matter for zero test).
3. If S==0 -> 0. Else if (r-l+1) odd -> 1 (removing one suitable rod always works: the running sum changes by +-1 steps). Else -> 2 (remove last rod to get odd length, then 1 more).
dry_run:
Sample test 3: s=+-+-, p=[0,1,2,3,4].
Query(1,1): S=1, length 1 odd -> 1.
Query(1,2): S=2, even -> 2.
Query(2,3): S=p3-p1=2, even -> 2. Matches outputs 1,2,...,2.

brief: Array a (n<=1e5). Move: replace adjacent a_i,a_{i+1} by a_i-a_{i+1}, a_i+a_{i+1}. Min moves to make gcd of all > 1 (print YES and count).
key_idea: If gcd>1 already: 0. Otherwise make everything even: an (odd,odd) pair costs 1 move, an (odd,even) pair costs 2.
solution:
1. g = gcd of all; if g>1 print YES 0.
2. Applying the move twice gives (-2a_{i+1}, 2a_i) -> both even; a move on two odds gives two even numbers.
3. Scan left to right: if a_i odd and a_{i+1} odd: ans+=1, mark both even; else if a_i odd (next even): ans+=2, mark even.
4. Last element odd handled by pairing with previous (scan i up to n-1 with a_{i+1}; for i=n, pair with i-1 -> +2).
5. Always possible: print YES and ans.
complexity: O(n log A) time, O(1) extra space
dry_run:
Sample 1: [1,1]: gcd=1. i=1: both odd -> ans=1. Output YES 1.
Sample 3: [1,3]: both odd -> 1.
Own: [1,2]: odd,even -> 2.

brief: Token at cell n must reach cell 1; from x you may move to x-y (1<=y<x) or floor(x/z) (2<=z<=x), each choice distinct. Count ways mod m (n<=2e5).
key_idea: f[x] = ways from x to 1 = (sum f[1..x-1]) + sum_{z=2..x} f[x/z]; group equal floor(x/z) values in O(sqrt x) blocks.
solution:
1. f[1]=1, prefix S[x]=f[1]+..+f[x].
2. For x=2..n: f[x] = S[x-1] + sum over blocks of z with same q=x/z: (z_hi - z_lo + 1) * f[q], where z_hi = x/q.
3. Update S[x]. All mod m (use long long).
4. Answer f[n].
complexity: O(n sqrt n) time, O(n) space

brief: Permutation a. Array is cool if no interior element is larger than both neighbors. Op: pick a peak (larger than both neighbors) and delete one of its neighbors. Min ops to make array cool.
key_idea: Recurse on the Cartesian tree (max-rooted): in a segment, its max must end up at one side, so delete everything on one side of it and recurse into the other.
solution:
1. Build max-Cartesian tree with a monotonic stack.
2. For a segment with max at q, left part size L, right part size R: F = min(L + F(right child), R + F(left child)). (Keep max; it eats one whole side, the other side is recursively made into a valley bounded by larger values.)
3. F(empty)=0, single element = 0.
4. Evaluate in post-order iteratively (n up to 5e5, avoid deep recursion). Answer F(root).

brief: A sequence is generated from a start sequence by repeatedly inserting (x+1) right after some element x. f(b)=min start length to produce b. Sum f over all subarrays of a (n<=3e5).
key_idea: b_i can be generated iff its nearest previous strictly smaller element (inside the subarray) has value b_i-1; count per-element contributions.
solution:
1. For each i find p_i = nearest j<i with a_j < a_i (monotonic stack), 0 if none (1-indexed).
2. If p_i exists and a[p_i]==a_i-1, i is 'original' only for subarrays with l in (p_i, i]; else for all l in [1,i].
3. Contribution = (i - L) * (n - i + 1), where L = p_i in first case, else 0.
4. Sum in long long.

brief: Alice/Bob see episodes a_i/b_i on day i. In a day range [L,R] each starts having seen nothing and watches the day's episode only if it is the next one they need. Range is valid if every day both watch the same episode or neither watches. Count valid ranges (n<=5e5).
key_idea: While valid, both counters stay equal (c); only 'event' days where a_i or b_i equals c+1 matter, so precompute for each matched day the furthest valid end via jumps.
solution:
1. Validity is prefix-closed, so answer = sum over L of (maxR(L)-L+1).
2. pos[w] = sorted days i where a_i==w or b_i==w. After a matched day j (a_j==b_j=v, counter becomes v), next event k = first day in pos[v+1] greater than j.
3. f[j] (furthest valid R after advancing at j): no k -> n; a_k==b_k -> f[k]; else k-1. Compute j from n down to 1.
4. For L: k = first day >= L in pos[1]; none -> maxR=n; a_k==b_k==1 -> f[k]; else k-1.
5. Sum (maxR-L+1) in long long.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Sample 1: a=[1,2,1], b=[1,2,2].
f[2]: v=2, no day with value 3 after 2 -> 3. f[1]: v=1, next value-2 day is 2 (matched) -> f[2]=3.
L=1: first value-1 day is 1 (matched) -> R=3: 3 ranges. L=2: first value-1 day>=2 is 3 (a=1,b=2 mismatch) -> R=2: 1. L=3: R=2: 0.
Total 4.

brief: Given the sign string s ('+','-','0') of prefix sums of an unknown array of nonzero integers, find the minimum possible max |a_i|, or -1 if impossible.
key_idea: Prefix p_i must change every step; answer is only -1/1/2/3 depending on runs of equal signs and their neighbours.
solution:
1. -1 if s[0]=='0' or two consecutive '0' (p would not change).
2. Treat position 0 as a '0'. Split into maximal runs of '+' or '-'; each run can start/end at +-1 when allowed.
3. If a run touches an opposite sign (jump from >=1 to <=-1): ans>=2.
4. If a run is bounded by '0'/start on the left and '0' on the right and its length is even: ans>=2 (cost 1 forces values 1,2,1,2,.. to alternate parity).
5. If a run of length exactly 2 has opposite signs on both sides: ans=3. Otherwise base ans=1.
dry_run:
Sample '+--+': run '--' (len 2) has '+' on both sides -> 3.
'+---+': run len 3 -> values 1,-1,-2,-1,1 -> 2.
'++0': run '++' bounded by start and '0', even -> 2 (p=1,2,0).
'+': run ends at string end -> 1.

brief: n<=100 books with thickness t_i in {1,2} and width w_i. Upright books' total thickness must be >= total width of the books lying on top. Minimize total thickness of upright books.
key_idea: Condition sum_t(V) >= W_total - sum_w(V); knapsack dp[T] = max total width of upright books with thickness T.
solution:
1. W = sum of all widths, Tmax = sum of thicknesses (<=200).
2. dp[T] = max sum w over subsets with thickness exactly T (-inf if impossible), dp[0]=0; 0/1 knapsack iterate T downwards.
3. Answer = min T with dp[T] >= 0 and T + dp[T] >= W.
4. Choosing all books always works (T=Tmax).
complexity: O(n * sum t) time, O(sum t) space

brief: String s (n<=1e3); letter x may only appear in pieces of length <= a_x. Split s into pieces: output number of splittings mod 1e9+7, max possible piece length, min number of pieces.
key_idea: Classic partition DP: for each end i scan start j backwards while length <= min limit of letters in s[j..i].
solution:
1. ways[0]=1, mn[0]=0; for i=1..n: lim=INF; for j=i down to 1: lim=min(lim, a[s_j]); if i-j+1>lim break.
2. ways[i]+=ways[j-1]; mn[i]=min(mn[i], mn[j-1]+1); best=max(best, i-j+1).
3. Every valid piece is reachable since the prefix before it is always splittable (single chars are always valid as a_x>=1).
4. Print ways[n], best, mn[n].
dry_run:
Sample s=aab, a=2,b=3.
i=1: 'a' -> ways1=1, mn1=1.
i=2: 'a' (from 1), 'aa' (len2<=2) -> ways2=2, mn2=1, best=2.
i=3: 'b' -> +2; 'ab' (lim 2) -> +1; 'aab' len3>2 stop -> ways3=3, mn3=2.
Output 3 / 2 / 2.

brief: Count ordered pairs of positive integers (a,b) with a+b=s and a xor b=x (s,x<=1e12).
key_idea: a+b = (a^b) + 2(a&b): AND is fixed as d=(s-x)/2; each set bit of x can go to a or b freely.
solution:
1. If s<x or (s-x) odd -> 0.
2. d=(s-x)/2; if d & x != 0 -> 0 (a bit can't be both in AND and XOR).
3. ans = 2^popcount(x).
4. If d==0, the pairs (0,x),(x,0) are invalid (need positive) -> ans -= 2.
5. Use 64-bit; popcount via __builtin_popcountll.
dry_run:
Sample s=9, x=5: d=(9-5)/2=2; 2&5=0 ok.
popcount(5)=2 -> 4 pairs; d!=0 so no subtraction.
Output 4 ((2,7),(3,6),(6,3),(7,2)).

brief: An x-y counter starts at 0, prints its last digit, then adds x or y. Given printed string s (starts with '0', |s|<=2e6) with some digits erased, for every 0<=x,y<=9 output the min number of digits to insert (or -1), as a 10x10 table.
key_idea: Only consecutive digit pairs matter: count cnt[a][b]; for each (x,y) BFS over 10 digit states gives min steps between digits.
solution:
1. cnt[a][b] = number of adjacent pairs (s_i, s_{i+1}) - at most 100 kinds.
2. For each (x,y): dist[a][b] = min number of additions (>=1) to go from digit a to digit b, moving a->(a+x)%10 or (a+y)%10 (BFS/Floyd on 10 nodes).
3. Answer = sum cnt[a][b]*(dist[a][b]-1); if some cnt>0 has dist=INF -> -1.
4. Note a->a needs >=1 step (cycle), so compute dist as shortest path with at least one edge.

brief: Columns of heights a_i (n<=2e5); gravity pushes every cube right within its own row. You may remove one top cube first (or not). Maximize total distance moved.
key_idea: Rows are independent: row h has c_h cubes that pack into columns n-c_h+1..n. Removing the top cube of column i only changes row a_i, by i - (n - c_{a_i} + 1).
solution:
1. c_h = #{i : a_i >= h}, S_h = sum of such indices i (suffix sums over value buckets).
2. Base = sum_h [ (sum of n-c_h+1..n) - S_h ].
3. Removing top cube of column i (row h=a_i): the cube that occupied the leftmost final slot n-c_h+1 disappears, so delta_i = i - (n-c_h+1).
4. Answer = base + max(0, max_i delta_i). Use long long.

brief: Rooted tree (root 1); leaves hold distinct values 1..k. Children start in increasing index order and you may cyclically rotate any vertex's child list. Can leaves (left to right) become 1,2,...,k?
key_idea: Every subtree's leaves must form a contiguous value range; at each node the children's ranges, read in index order, must chain consecutively after some cyclic rotation.
solution:
1. Build children lists (iterate i=2..n so lists are in index order); get a BFS order to process bottom-up.
2. Leaf: lo=hi=a_v, cnt=1. Internal: lo=min, hi=max of children, cnt=sum.
3. Require hi-lo+1 == cnt (contiguous).
4. Start from the child with smallest lo and walk cyclically: each next child's lo must equal previous child's hi+1; else NO.
5. If all nodes pass -> YES.
dry_run:
Own example: root 1 with children 2,3 (leaves) values a2=2,a3=1.
Ranges: child2=[2,2], child3=[1,1]. Smallest lo is child3; cyclic order 3,2: lo(2)=2=hi(3)+1 ok -> YES (rotate once).
If root had leaves 3,1,2 in index order: start at value 1 -> 2 -> then 3 cyclically: YES; order 2,1,3 -> 1,3 fails -> NO.

brief: Tree with n<=2e5 nodes, stone on start node (activated). Players alternate moving it to an adjacent non-activated node; Ron moves first; who can't move loses. Print winner.
key_idea: Root the tree at the start; a node is winning for the player to move iff some child is losing (moving away from root only, since visited nodes block going back).
solution:
1. Root at start u; moves always go to an unvisited neighbor = a child.
2. win[v] = OR over children c of !win[c]; leaves are losing.
3. Compute with iterative DFS order (avoid recursion depth 2e5).
4. Print Ron if win[u] else Hermione.
dry_run:
Sample: edges 1-2,1-3,3-4,3-5, start 1.
Leaves 2,4,5: lose. Node 3: children 4,5 losing -> win.
Node 1: child 2 is losing -> win -> Ron.

brief: Decimal grade string (length<=2e5) and t<=1e9 roundings; each rounding can be at any position after the point or to an integer. Output the max grade (no trailing zeros).
key_idea: Round at the first fractional digit >=5; the carry may create a new 5 one place left, so keep rounding while t lasts.
solution:
1. Find the first index i after '.' with digit >= '5'; if none, print s.
2. While t>0 and i is after the '.' and s[i]>='5': cut s to length i, t--, i--; if s[i]=='.', carry into integer part and stop; else s[i]++ (digits before i are <5 so no 9-overflow here).
3. If carry into integer: drop '.' and fraction, add 1 to the integer string propagating 9s (may prepend '1').
4. Print s (never ends with '.' since that case becomes the integer case).
dry_run:
Sample n=6,t=1, s=10.245.
First digit>=5 after '.' is '5' (index 5).
Round: cut to 10.24, increment -> 10.25, t=0. Stop.
Output 10.25 (with t=2 we'd get 10.3).

brief: A day has n hours and m minutes (<=1e9); hours shown with the min number of base-7 digits needed for n-1, minutes for m-1 (leading zeros). Count (h,m) pairs whose displayed digits are all distinct.
key_idea: Total digits > 7 means 0 answers (only 7 base-7 digits); otherwise n*m <= 7^7, so brute force all pairs.
solution:
1. dh = number of base-7 digits of n-1 (at least 1), dm likewise for m-1.
2. If dh+dm > 7 print 0.
3. Else for each h<n, m'<m: write h with dh digits and m' with dm digits in base 7 and check all digits distinct (bitmask of used digits).
4. Count valid pairs (at most 7^7 ~ 8e5 pairs).

brief: Melody a_1..a_n (n<=1e5). Assign fingers 1..5: if next note is higher the finger must be higher, lower -> lower, equal -> different. Output any valid fingering or -1.
key_idea: dp[i][f] = can note i use finger f; transitions over 5x5 finger pairs, store parent to reconstruct.
solution:
1. dp[0][f]=true for all f.
2. For i>=1, f, g: dp[i][g] |= dp[i-1][f] if (a_i>a_{i-1} and g>f) or (a_i<a_{i-1} and g<f) or (a_i==a_{i-1} and g!=f); store par[i][g]=f.
3. If no dp[n-1][g] true -> -1.
4. Else backtrack through par and print.
dry_run:
Sample a=1 1 4 2 2.
i=1 equal: any g with some f!=g -> all 5 ok.
i=2 rising: g>=2 ok. i=3 falling: g<=4 ok. i=4 equal: all ok.
Backtrack e.g. 1 4 5 4 5 (valid).

brief: Each day the water level gets a mark (unless one exists at that height). m_i = marks strictly above water on day i. Minimize sum of d_i = marks strictly below water.
key_idea: Let t_i = total marks after day i: d_i = t_i - m_i - 1. Need t_i >= m_i+1, t non-decreasing, increments <= 1; take the smallest such t.
solution:
1. Forward: t_i = max(t_{i-1}, m_i+1).
2. Backward: t_i = max(t_i, t_{i+1}-1) (can't add more than one mark per day).
3. This is the pointwise minimal feasible t.
4. Answer = sum (t_i - m_i - 1) in long long.
dry_run:
Sample m=0 1 0 3 0 2.
Forward t: 1 2 2 4 4 4. Backward: 1 2 3 4 4 4.
d = 0 0 2 0 3 1 -> sum 6.

brief: Array a, integer k, moduli p<q. Op: pick a segment of length >= k and replace each element by a_i mod p (or mod q). Minimize the final sum.
key_idea: Each element ends as v1=a%p or v3=(a%q)%p: v3 needs a q-op before its last p-op and no earlier p-op. Achievable v3-sets are runs that are either long (>=k) or adjacent to a non-v3 gap of length >= k.
solution:
1. Order ops: early p-ops (P1), then q-ops (Q), then one p-op on the whole array. Element gets v3 iff in Q and not in P1, else v1.
2. So S (v3 positions) = Q minus P1: each maximal S-run has length>=k or an adjacent gap (non-S run) of length>=k.
3. Block DP over prefix with states: gapBig, gapSmall (last block a gap of len>=k / <k), runOK, runNeed (short run whose left gap was small; next gap must be big). Start acts as runOK for gaps and gapSmall for runs.
4. Transitions use prefix sums of v1/v3 with 'j<=i-k' prefix minima and 'i-k<j<i' sliding-window minima (deques).
5. Answer min(gapBig[n], gapSmall[n], runOK[n]).

brief: DAG (n<=100) with lowercase letters on edges; two marbles, Max moves first, players alternate moving their own marble; each move's letter must be >= previous move's letter. Player unable to move loses. Output winner table for all start pairs.
key_idea: State (my vertex, opponent vertex, last letter): I win if some outgoing edge with letter >= last leads to a losing state for the opponent.
solution:
1. win(v,u,c) = true iff exists edge v->w with letter l>=c and win(u,w,l) is false (roles swap).
2. The graph is a DAG so recursion terminates; memoize over 100*100*26 states.
3. Answer cell (i,j) = 'A' if win(i,j,'a') else 'B'.
4. Each state iterates over v's outgoing edges.
complexity: O(n^2 * 26 * deg) time, O(26 n^2) space
dry_run:
Sample: edges 1->2 b, 1->3 a, 2->4 c, 3->4 b.
(i=1,j=1): Max moves 1->2 'b'; Lucas at 1 needs letter>='b': 1->2 'b'; Max at 2 plays 2->4 'c'; Lucas at 2 plays 2->4 'c'; Max at 4 stuck -> Max loses this line; table says (1,1)=B.
Row 4 all 'B' (Max can't move from 4).

brief: a_2..a_n given; for each a_1=i (1..n-1) run: x=1,y=0; repeat {y+=a_x, x+=a_x; then y+=a_x, x-=a_x} until x<=0 or x>n. Print final y or -1 if infinite.
key_idea: State (x, next step type) for x>=2 has a fixed outcome; memoize y-gain with cycle detection. Returning to x=1 always happens before an add step -> infinite.
solution:
1. After the first step from x=1: x=1+i, y=i, next step is 'subtract'.
2. val[x][d] = total y added from state (x, d) until exit, -1 if infinite: nx = x+a_x (d=0) or x-a_x (d=1); out of range -> a_x; nx==1 -> -1; else a_x + val[nx][1-d] (or -1).
3. Compute iteratively (explicit stack, 4e5 states) with colors; meeting an in-progress state = cycle -> -1.
4. Answer i: val[1+i][1]==-1 ? -1 : i + val[1+i][1]. Use long long.

brief: n<=100 days; animal arriving on day i eats c_i tons every day from i to n if accepted. Start with X tons; accept as many animals as possible without running out. (Old round: read input.txt, write output.txt.)
key_idea: Accepted animal i costs c_i*(n-i+1) in total; maximize count under budget X -> take cheapest totals first.
solution:
1. cost_i = c_i * (n - i + 1) (1-indexed).
2. Sort costs ascending; take while running sum <= X.
3. Feeding is cumulative so only total consumption matters (food never replenishes).
4. This problem uses files input.txt / output.txt.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Sample n=3, X=4, c=1 1 1: costs 3,2,1.
Sorted 1,2,3: take 1 (sum1), 2 (sum3), 3 would make 6>4.
Answer 2.

brief: 2 x n grid with free cells '.' and blocked '#'. Decide whether free cells can be tiled by dominoes in exactly one way (Unique), several (Multiple) or none (None).
key_idea: Column profile DP over which cells of the current column are already filled by horizontal dominoes from the left; count tilings capped at 2.
solution:
1. dp[mask] = number of tilings (capped at 2) with mask = cells of column i already covered by horizontals from column i-1.
2. For column i: occ = blocked bits; if occ & mask -> invalid. free = ~(occ|mask) & 3.
3. free==0 -> next 0; free==1 or 2 -> must go horizontal: next = free; free==3 -> vertical (next 0) or two horizontals (next 3).
4. Saturate counts at 2. After the last column only mask 0 is valid.
5. Print None / Unique / Multiple for dp=0/1/2.
dry_run:
Sample 4: n=3, all '#': every column free=0, dp[0]=1 -> Unique (empty tiling).
Sample 3: 2x8 all free -> many tilings -> Multiple.
Own: 2x1 all free: free=3 -> vertical (mask0) or horizontals (mask3, invalid at end) -> Unique.

brief: n x m grid of 0/1 (n,m<=400). A portal is an a x b sub-rectangle (a>=5,b>=4) whose non-corner border cells are 1, interior cells 0, corners arbitrary. Min cell flips to create a portal.
key_idea: Fix top row i and bottom row j; sweep right border r and keep the best left border l<=r-3 via a running minimum of (side cost - prefix of middle cost).
solution:
1. Column prefix sums of ones: ones(c, r1..r2) in O(1).
2. For rows i<j with j>=i+4: side(c) = zeros in column c rows i+1..j-1; mid(c) = (a[i][c]==0) + (a[j][c]==0) + ones in rows i+1..j-1.
3. P[c] = prefix sum of mid. cost(l,r) = side(l) + (P[r-1]-P[l]) + side(r).
4. Sweep r from 3: add candidate l=r-3 into best=min(best, side(l)-P[l]); cost = best + P[r-1] + side(r).
5. Take global min.
dry_run:
Sample 1 (5x4, only one rectangle): sides need 3 ones each in cols 1,4 (rows 2-4): col1 has 0 ones -> 3, col4 0 -> 3.
Middle cols 2,3: top row needs 1s (both 0 -> 2), bottom (both 0 -> 2), interior must be 0: row3 has '11' -> 2.
Total 3+3+2+2+2 = 12.

brief: Binary strings x' and y' of length n; y must be the prefix-parity string of x (y_i = parity of ones in x_1..x_i). Min total bit flips in x' and y' to make that true.
key_idea: Scan left to right tracking the prefix parity; choose each x_i (0/1), paying for flipping x_i and for y_i mismatching the new parity.
solution:
1. dp[p] = min flips so far with current prefix parity p; dp[0]=0, dp[1]=INF.
2. For each i and choice b in {0,1}: q=p^b, cost = (b!=x'_i) + (q!=y'_i); nd[q]=min(nd[q], dp[p]+cost).
3. Answer min(dp[0],dp[1]).
4. Total length up to 1e6: use fast IO.
dry_run:
Sample 2: x'=11101, y'=10010.
Keeping x: parities 1,0,1,1,0 vs y' 1,0,0,1,0 -> 1 mismatch (pos 3).
DP finds nothing cheaper -> 1.

brief: Given x<=100, find the smallest n such that some n x n 0/1 matrix has exactly x ones, no two ones edge-adjacent, and is symmetric under horizontal and vertical reflection.
key_idea: Use odd n: max ones is (n^2+1)/2 (checkerboard) and every count up to it is reachable thanks to the symmetric 4-groups/2-groups - except x=3 which needs n=5.
solution:
1. If x==3 answer 5 (n=3 can hold 1,2,4,5 ones but not 3).
2. Otherwise iterate odd n=1,3,5,...: answer is the first n with (n*n+1)/2 >= x.
3. Even n is never better: symmetry forces the central 2x2 block cells to be equal -> adjacent ones impossible near the centre, capacity too small.
dry_run:
Sample x=4: n=1 cap 1; n=3 cap 5 >= 4 -> 3.
Sample x=9: n=3 cap 5 < 9; n=5 cap 13 >= 9 -> 5.
x=3 -> special case 5.

brief: Stops 0..n (n<=1e9), m<=1e5 buses; bus i goes s_i->t_i, can be boarded at any stop in [s_i, t_i-1] and left only at t_i. Count ways to get from 0 to n mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: ways(bus i) = [s_i==0] + sum of ways of buses whose end t_j lies in [s_i, t_i-1]; sort buses by t and use prefix sums + binary search.
solution:
1. Sort buses by t. Process in order; maintain prefix sums of ways over the sorted list.
2. For bus i: the buses with t_j in [s_i, t_i-1] form a contiguous index range among those already processed (find with lower_bound on t).
3. w_i = (s_i==0) + sum over that range (mod).
4. Answer = sum of w_i over buses with t_i==n; 0 if none.
complexity: O(m log m) time, O(m) space

brief: Strings s,t (<=5000). Count pairs (x,y): x a substring of s (by position), y a subsequence of t (by indices), with equal content. Mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: dp[i][j] = pairs where substring ends at s_i and subsequence uses t-indices up to j with its last char matched inside t[1..j].
solution:
1. dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-1] + (s_i==t_j ? 1 + dp[i-1][j-1] : 0).
   (1 = the single-char pair; dp[i-1][j-1] extends every pair ending at s_{i-1} with subsequence ending before j.)
2. Answer = sum over i of dp[i][|t|].
3. Keep two rows of length |t|+1; mod each step.

brief: Given A,B (0..2^64-1), find non-negative X,Y with X+Y=A and X xor Y=B, minimizing X; print -1 if impossible.
key_idea: X+Y = (X^Y) + 2(X&Y), so X&Y = (A-B)/2; the minimum X takes only the AND bits.
solution:
1. If A<B or (A-B) odd -> -1.
2. D=(A-B)/2; if D & B != 0 -> -1 (bit can't be in both AND and XOR).
3. X = D, Y = D + B (= A - D).
4. Use unsigned long long for 64-bit range.

brief: Words start and end (length 2..1000) and k<=1e5. A split turns w=xy into yx (x,y nonempty). Count ways to turn start into end with exactly k splits, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: A split is a rotation by r in 1..n-1; track only 'total rotation 0' vs 'a specific nonzero rotation' (all nonzero rotations are symmetric).
solution:
1. a = ways current total rotation is 0, b = ways it equals one particular nonzero value. Start a=1,b=0.
2. Each step: a' = (n-1)*b; b' = a + (n-2)*b (mod).
3. After k steps: answer = sum over r in [0,n) with rotate(start,r)==end of (r==0 ? a : b).
4. Check rotations by comparing (start+start).substr(r,n) with end - O(n^2) fine.
dry_run:
Sample 2: start=end=ababab, k=1.
Step: a=0, b=1.
Rotations equal to end: r=0,2,4 -> a + b + b = 0+1+1 = 2.
Output 2.

brief: Masha's number s (<=50 digits). New number: first digit any 0..9; digit i = average of s_i and new digit i-1, rounded up or down when not integer. Count distinct new numbers, excluding s itself if it can be produced.
key_idea: dp[i][d] = number of ways (= distinct prefixes) with new digit d at position i; each choice sequence gives a different number.
solution:
1. dp[0][d]=1 for d=0..9.
2. For i>=1 and prev d: sum = s_i + d; if even -> dp[i][sum/2] += dp[i-1][d]; else add to both sum/2 and sum/2+1.
3. Total = sum dp[n-1][*] (use long long; up to 10*2^49).
4. Check if s itself is producible: for every i>=1, s_i must be floor or ceil of (s_i + s_{i-1})/2. If yes subtract 1.
complexity: O(10 n) time, O(10 n) space
dry_run:
Sample '09': d0 even (0,2,4,6,8) -> 9+d0 odd -> 2 choices each = 10; d0 odd -> 1 each = 5. Total 15.
Is '09' producible? (9+0)/2=4.5 -> 4 or 5, not 9 -> no subtraction. Output 15.

brief: n<=1000 friends, each a w_i x h_i rectangle that may be rotated. Photo width = sum of widths, height = max height. Minimize area.
key_idea: Fix the maximum height H (1..1000); each friend independently picks the orientation with height<=H and minimal width.
solution:
1. For H = 1..1000: total=0; for each friend, candidate widths: w if h<=H, h if w<=H; if none -> H infeasible; else add the min.
2. area = total * H; answer = min over feasible H.
3. The real max height may be < H, but then a smaller H gives a smaller area, so min is still correct.
(Note: the mirror version 529B adds a limit of n/2 rotations - not in this round version.)

brief: n balls, special one at position k; m swaps (x_i,y_i) in order, each may be faked (skipped). For every position p, min number of faked swaps so the special ball ends at p, or -1.
key_idea: dist[p] = min skips so far with ball at p; a swap (x,y) only changes dist[x] and dist[y]: perform (ball moves free) or fake (stays, +1).
solution:
1. dist[k]=0, others INF.
2. For each swap (x,y): nx = min(dist[x]+1, dist[y]); ny = min(dist[y]+1, dist[x]); assign simultaneously.
3. Other positions unchanged (a swap not touching p doesn't matter whether faked).
4. Print dist or -1 for INF.

brief: Bracket string s (n<=2e5) and binary a (length n-3): for each a_i=1, s_i..s_{i+3} must be a regular bracket sequence. Min single-bracket flips, or -1.
key_idea: Only '(())' and '()()' are regular of length 4; DP over the last 3 characters (8 states) and check the window when it closes.
solution:
1. dp[mask] over the last three chosen chars (bit=1 for '('), cost = number of flips.
2. At position i choose c in {'(',')'}: cost += (c != s_i); new window = last 3 + c.
3. If i>=3 and a_{i-3}=='1', the 4-char window must be (()) or ()(); otherwise reject.
4. Initialize by enumerating the first 3 chars (8 masks). Answer = min over masks at the end; INF -> -1.
dry_run: Sample 1: s='))((', a='1' -> window must be '(())' (cost 2: flip s1,s4... '))((' vs '(())': diffs at 1 and 4 = 2) or '()()' (diffs at 1 and 4? ')' vs '(' pos1, ')' ok pos2, '(' ok pos3, '(' vs ')' pos4 = 2). Answer 2.

brief: Tree with n<=50000 vertices and k<=500. Count unordered pairs of vertices at distance exactly k.
key_idea: dp[v][d] = number of vertices in v's subtree at depth d below v (d<=k); combine children at v counting pairs through v.
solution:
1. Root at 1; get a BFS order and process vertices in reverse (children first).
2. dp[v][0]=1. For each child c: first count ans += sum_{d=0..k-1} dp[c][d] * dp[v][k-1-d]; then merge dp[v][d+1] += dp[c][d].
3. Counting before merging ensures pairs come from different branches (or v itself).
4. Memory n*(k+1) ints (~100MB) is allowed (512MB); answer in long long.
complexity: O(n k) time, O(n k) space
